claims.statement: The NameAllocator class provides a context-scoped mechanism for generating Java identifiers that never conflict with existing names or reserved language keywords, using tag-based allocation and suffix-based collision disambiguation.

NameAllocator.newName(String suggestion, Object tag) validates the suggested name via toJavaIdentifier for character normalization and keyword protection, then appends underscores until a unique identifier is found.
Each tag must map to exactly one allocated name; attempting to allocate a second name under an already-bound tag throws IllegalArgumentException with a descriptive message.
TypeVariableName.bounds are stripped of java.lang.Object during emission since Java syntax omits redundant extends Object clauses.
WildcardTypeName emits fully qualified wildcard syntax: '?' when no bounds exist, '? extends X' for single upper bound, and '? super S' for single lower bound.
WildcardTypeName construction enforces that upper bounds are non-primitive and non-void, and exactly one upper bound is permitted per wildcard type.
NameAllocator uses LinkedHashSet for O(1) collision detection and LinkedHashMap for tag-to-name mapping, preserving insertion order for deterministic iteration.

Character normalization via toJavaIdentifier prefixes '_' for invalid start characters (digits or non-starters), replaces invalid intermediate characters with '_', and handles Unicode surrogate pairs.
